eintraege.name: 808 Classic 808
eintraege.text: Factory voicing: long round kick, low tom family, cowbell and clave on tap.

eintraege.name: 808 Electro Clave
eintraege.text: Cowbell and clave up front, tuned toms, short kick.

eintraege.name: 808 Long Boom
eintraege.text: Kick and boom (note 35) tuned very low with long decays; sub that carries a bar.

eintraege.name: 808 Miami Bass
eintraege.text: Low, long, driven kick with a short punch; open clap.

eintraege.name: 808 Tape Lo-fi
eintraege.text: Filtered, driven and soft: the filter sits left of centre, hats dark.

eintraege.name: 808 Tight Funk
eintraege.text: Short kick, snappy snare, very short hats: for fast syncopated patterns.

eintraege.name: 808 Trap
eintraege.text: Deep kick with a slow fall, tight rolling hats, snappy snare, long clap.

eintraege.name: 808 Zap Kit
eintraege.text: Kick, toms and snare with extreme pitch falls.

eintraege.name: 909 Berlin Techno
eintraege.text: Long, low kick with a hard click, driven; closed hats tight, open hat medium, snare dry and short on the snappy side.

eintraege.name: 909 DnB Tight
eintraege.text: High, short kick; bright, snappy snare; very short hats.

eintraege.name: 909 Dusty Boom Bap
eintraege.text: Low-passed kit: soft kick, loose snare, dark hats.

eintraege.name: 909 Goa
eintraege.text: Medium kick with a long pitch fall and a sharp click; bright hats with some noise; short clap.

eintraege.name: 909 Hard Industrial
eintraege.text: Overdriven kick and bus, loud click, noisy hats and a long crash.

eintraege.name: 909 House Classic
eintraege.text: Near the factory voicing: round kick, open clap, shuffling hats with a long open hat.

eintraege.name: 909 Rave Stab Toms
eintraege.text: Tuned toms as a melodic part: wide tom spacing, short decay, strong tom punch.

eintraege.name: 909 Zap Kit
eintraege.text: Kick, toms and snare with extreme pitch falls: laser and zap sounds, pitched up rim and toms.

eintraege.name: Hard Driven G1
eintraege.text: Hard driven kick tuned to G1 (49 Hz): heavy overdrive on the body, click on top, tail stays on the note.

eintraege.name: Long Sub G0
eintraege.text: Sub kick tuned to G0 (24.5 Hz) with a 2.2 s tail that carries the low end; barely any click.

eintraege.name: Punchy E1
eintraege.text: Short punchy kick tuned to E1 (41.2 Hz) with a fast pitch drop and a clear click.

eintraege.name: Saw Bass
eintraege.text: Plain saw bass: ladder at a low cutoff, a quick filter pluck on every note, full sustain, short release.

eintraege.name: Saw Pluck
eintraege.text: Short saw pluck: the filter envelope opens a low cutoff and closes again within 150 ms, no sustain.

eintraege.name: Soft Pad
eintraege.text: Slow saw pad: 200 ms attack, long release, the filter breathes open and settles over two seconds.

eintraege.name: Mono Acid 303
eintraege.text: TB-303 style line: diode filter, saw, short filter decay, high resonance, accent from velocity, 50 ms slide on overlapped notes.

eintraege.name: Mono DnB Sub
eintraege.text: Clean sine sub for drum and bass: triangle through a closed ladder, sine sub one octave down, full sustain, light drive.

eintraege.name: Mono Dub Bass
eintraege.text: Plucky house bass with a ping-pong delay at a dotted eighth, a short hall tail and a touch of chorus: the notes echo around a dry core.

eintraege.name: Mono Evolving Lead
eintraege.text: Pulse lead that opens slowly: the mod envelope sweeps the cutoff, a tempo-synced LFO 2 moves the pulse width every half note, chorus, delay and a little hall.

eintraege.name: Mono Goa Lead
eintraege.text: Bright goa line: two detuned saws, diode filter at high resonance, quick envelope bark, 120 ms glide, gentle vibrato.

eintraege.name: Mono Hoover Growl
eintraege.text: Hoover-like growl: saw and pulse with slow PWM, wide detune, osc 2 synced and swept down by the envelope, sub, glide into every note, SEM filter.

eintraege.name: Mono House Bass
eintraege.text: Plucky off-beat house bass: ladder, saw plus pulse an octave up, square sub, fast filter pluck that falls to a dark sustain.

eintraege.name: Mono MS-20 Screamer
eintraege.text: Two saws through the MS-20 filter at high resonance, driven, with a slow triangle LFO opening and closing the scream.

eintraege.name: Mono Rolling Techno Bass
eintraege.text: Constant low rolling bass for off-beat 16ths: ladder, saw plus detuned pulse, square sub, small filter pluck, tight amp.

eintraege.name: Mono Sync Lead
eintraege.text: Hard-sync lead: osc 2 locked to osc 1 and swept by the filter envelope (Sync = Sweep), ladder filter, light vibrato.

eintraege.name: Neuro Classic Reese
eintraege.text: Three detuned saws through a slow low-pass, a touch of fold for edge and a round sub underneath.

eintraege.name: Neuro Deep Rumble
eintraege.text: The dark rolling bass with a feedback delay and a long hall behind it, a shorter amp decay and some key follow: a rumble that echoes away.

eintraege.name: Neuro Fold Scream
eintraege.text: The wavefolder pushed hard and off centre, followed by a diode low-pass that is envelope-driven: screaming harmonics that decay each note.

eintraege.name: Neuro Fold Talker
eintraege.text: The vowel bass with a second LFO breathing the wavefolder on every eighth note, a sine one octave down under the saws and some velocity.

eintraege.name: Neuro Goa Zap
eintraege.text: FM and ring modulation at a high ratio, a diode filter that snaps shut on every sixteenth and a sample-and-hold flutter: rubbery psytrance bass.

eintraege.name: Neuro Neuro Growl
eintraege.text: Folded and FM-driven saws into a resonant low-pass that swings every eighth note: the classic wet growl.

eintraege.name: Neuro Notch Sweep
eintraege.text: A resonant notch sweeping through a wide detuned saw stack; hollow and phasing, slow, with a bright start of each note.

eintraege.name: Neuro Sub only
eintraege.text: Pure sub sine, mono, nothing above it: the foundation for layering.

eintraege.name: Neuro Talking Bass
eintraege.text: The vowel filter walks through the vowels every quarter note, with an envelope that opens each note on an a.

eintraege.name: Neuro Techno Rumble Bass
eintraege.text: A dark, driven short bass with a heavy sub, a closed filter that pumps on sixteenths and almost no width.

eintraege.name: Poly Brass
eintraege.text: Five saws at 7 cent through the ladder; the filter swells with the 80 ms attack and settles at 60 percent; light vibrato.

eintraege.name: Poly Detroit Strings
eintraege.text: Five saws at 14 cent, SEM low-pass, slow swell and chorus I at full: a string ensemble in the Juno manner; the LFO breathes the cutoff.

eintraege.name: Poly DnB Atmosphere
eintraege.text: Seven saws, 30 cent, full width; SEM drifting towards the notch with a very slow LFO on the cutoff; breath of noise.

eintraege.name: Poly Goa Lead Stack
eintraege.text: Seven saws at 14 cent plus a pulse; the diode ladder with high resonance and a fast filter decay; vibrato at 5.5 Hz, a little PWM on the pulse.

eintraege.name: Poly House Chord Stab
eintraege.text: Five saws at 9 cent with a square and a sub; SEM low-pass, short envelope, resonance 0.45; short chords on the off-beat.

eintraege.name: Poly Juno Pad
eintraege.text: Three saws, a pulse with slow PWM and a sub through the 24 dB ladder, chorus I at full: the 106 recipe.

eintraege.name: Poly Pluck
eintraege.text: Three saws at 6 cent with a pulse; ladder, envelope closes in 0.25 s to nothing, amplitude plucks with it.

eintraege.name: Poly Slow Sweep Pad
eintraege.text: Five saws and a second oscillator an octave down; LFO 2 opens and closes the cutoff once per bar, locked to the tempo (the channel reverb adds the room).

eintraege.name: Poly Sync Lead
eintraege.text: Three saws and a hard-synced second oscillator 7 ct sharp; the mod envelope sweeps its pitch up 14 st and back in 0.9 s, with a 50 ms glide and vibrato.

eintraege.name: Poly Trance Supersaw
eintraege.text: Seven saws, 25 cent, wide; SEM low-pass opens with a 0.5 s envelope; slow release, light chorus II.

eintraege.name: Chor Reverse Sigh
eintraege.text: Choir that starts on the last vowel and sighs back toward the first as the wave envelope falls.

eintraege.name: Chor Vowel Bloom
eintraege.text: Choir pad that opens from the first vowel to the last as each note blooms; the wave envelope sweeps the vowel table over about a second.

eintraege.name: Reese Sine Collapse
eintraege.text: Reese bass whose wave envelope starts at the sine and returns to the saw: a soft thump at the start of every note, then the full growl.

eintraege.name: Reese Square Punch
eintraege.text: Reese bass with a hollow square-wave punch on the attack that decays into the saw.

eintraege.name: Supersaw Morph Stab
eintraege.text: Wide supersaw that snaps from the saw into a square-wave stack on each note and relaxes back; chord stabs with a moving edge.

eintraege.name: Supersaw Triangle Swell
eintraege.text: Slow supersaw swell: the wave envelope rises over a second from a soft triangle blend and settles on the saw.

eintraege.name: Air Shelf
eintraege.text: A gentle high shelf above 11 kHz opens hats and pads without the fatigue of a presence boost.

eintraege.name: Dark Room
eintraege.text: Rolls off the top twice: a shelf at 7 kHz and a 24 dB/oct high cut at 10 kHz for a distant, dark tone.

eintraege.name: De-Box
eintraege.text: Cuts the 250-600 Hz region that Snoman calls the main culprit for muddy mixes, with the natural one-octave Q.

eintraege.name: Kick Cleanup
eintraege.text: High-pass at 30 Hz in the mid channel plus 2 dB of low shelf at 60 Hz keeps the weight and removes rumble.

eintraege.name: Low Mid Warmth
eintraege.text: A single wide bell at 150 Hz adds body in the sense of the vocabulary: fullness around 100-200 Hz.

eintraege.name: Mix Bus Tilt
eintraege.text: One dB of low shelf, one dB of high shelf and a small dip at 400 Hz: a tilt for the whole mix.

eintraege.name: Notch Ring
eintraege.text: A very narrow notch at 800 Hz removes one ringing partial without touching its neighbours.

eintraege.name: Presence Lead
eintraege.text: Two dB at 3 kHz bring a lead forward, a narrow cut at 7 kHz keeps it from turning harsh.

eintraege.name: Side Tame
eintraege.text: Cuts the low middle in the side channel only, so the bass stays centred and the mix stays mono-compatible.

eintraege.name: Telephone
eintraege.text: Band-limits the signal to a telephone band and lifts the middle so it cuts through the mix.

eintraege.name: Thin Out
eintraege.text: Removes the body below 200 Hz and dips the low mids so the part sits behind the bass.

eintraege.name: Ambient Bed
eintraege.text: An eight second tail with a slow low decay turns the reverb into a pad of its own.

eintraege.name: Big Drop
eintraege.text: A long pre-delay and a four second tail make the drop feel much larger than the room.

eintraege.name: Dark Dub
eintraege.text: Heavily damped highs over a long low tail: the reverb becomes a dark, wet space.

eintraege.name: Freeze Transition
eintraege.text: Freeze holds the last tail as a drone, so the reverb itself bridges the two tracks.

eintraege.name: Granular Tail
eintraege.text: Low diffusion and a 512 sample frame make the tail grainy, almost like clustered echoes.

eintraege.name: Metallic Perc
eintraege.text: A short frame and a long high decay give percussion a ringing, metallic space.

eintraege.name: Plate Sheen
eintraege.text: Bright, dense and wide: a plate-like sheen for leads and vocals with the lows kept out.

eintraege.name: Small Room
eintraege.text: A short, narrow room that puts the drums in a space without washing them out.

eintraege.name: Snare Space
eintraege.text: Early reflections carry the space, the tail is ducked: a snare hears a room without any wash.

eintraege.name: Subtle Glue
eintraege.text: A quiet, transparent send that glues a bus together without being heard as reverb.

eintraege.name: Vocal Hall
eintraege.text: A long pre-delay lets the word through first, then a warm hall fills the space behind it.

eintraege.name: Bass
eintraege.text: Fast attack that evens out the bass level so the low end sits steady under the kick.

eintraege.name: Bus Glue
eintraege.text: Gentle 2:1 compression with a long release that glues a bus without audible pumping.

eintraege.name: Drum Bus
eintraege.text: Medium ratio with a slow attack that lets transients through and holds the drum group together.

eintraege.name: Kick Sidechain
eintraege.text: Keyed from the external sidechain input with a fast attack so the channel ducks and pumps on every kick.

eintraege.name: Lead
eintraege.text: Moderate 3:1 control that keeps a lead line present and even in front of the mix.

eintraege.name: Parallel
eintraege.text: Hard 10:1 squash blended at 40 percent under the dry signal for density without losing transients.

eintraege.name: Bright Open
eintraege.text: An almost open filter turns the 303 voice into a thin, bright lead rather than a bass.

eintraege.name: Classic Acid
eintraege.text: Welsh acid patch: 450 Hz cutoff, 60 percent resonance, no envelope, cutoff played by hand.

eintraege.name: Dark Dub
eintraege.text: A square wave under a low cutoff: hollow, dark bass with a soft attack on the filter.

eintraege.name: Rolling Long
eintraege.text: Long decay and gentle resonance give the rolling, overlapping bass of trance and tech house.

eintraege.name: Screaming Acid
eintraege.text: Almost full resonance and a deep sweep: the line screams and the accents cut like a whip.

eintraege.name: Self Oscillation
eintraege.text: At full resonance the filter is a sine oscillator: the pitch is set by the cutoff knob.

eintraege.name: Square Lead
eintraege.text: A resonant square lead with a short filter sweep: nasal, cutting, monophonic.

eintraege.name: Squelch Acid
eintraege.text: High resonance plus a deep envelope sweep gives the squelching, chirping acid line.

eintraege.name: Stab Pluck
eintraege.text: A quarter second decay and a fast filter sweep make a short, percussive stab.

eintraege.name: Sub Bass
eintraege.text: Nearly closed filter with little resonance: weight and pitch, no movement.

eintraege.name: Acid Bite
eintraege.text: Heavy drive turns a 303 line into a biting, metallic lead without a second device.

eintraege.name: Bass Audibility
eintraege.text: Fifteen dB of drive fills the midrange with harmonics so the bass reads on a phone speaker.

eintraege.name: Bus Sheen
eintraege.text: Three dB into the curve at a quarter wet: a hint of density on a whole bus.

eintraege.name: Full Distortion
eintraege.text: The whole range into the curve: the signal becomes a hard, bright wall of harmonics.

eintraege.name: Kick Density
eintraege.text: Audible edge on the kick that survives small speakers, blended so the sub stays clean.

eintraege.name: Light Glue
eintraege.text: Four dB into the curve at 30 percent: enough shared harmonics for a bus to cohere.

eintraege.name: Pad Warmth
eintraege.text: A light touch of drive under a pad adds body while the clean signal keeps the softness.

eintraege.name: Parallel Drums
eintraege.text: Parallel distortion at 40 percent thickens a drum bus while the transients stay untouched.

eintraege.name: Snare Presence
eintraege.text: Harmonics on the transient make a snare cut through a dense mix.

eintraege.name: Tame Lead
eintraege.text: Half wet drive rounds off a too-clean lead and gives it weight in the midrange.
